title: [VIC] 30kWh Battery+10kW Inverter $5,799, 26.6kWh+5kW Inverter $5,299 (Garage Installation Recommended) @ PA Power
body:
Deal: [VIC] 30kWh Battery+10kW Inverter $5,799, 26.6kWh+5kW Inverter $5,299 (Garage Installation Recommended) @ PA Power

[SeanConnery] Not much of a deal compared to your past offers and very similar price to lots of quotes I've gotten from others also in Melbourne.
[MilkteaS] For size wise, yes. This deal is more about smaller houser owner who wants to install batteries in their garage.
If you are keen for bigger size or nice features… Sep/ October definitely worth waiting.
[SeanConnery] New shipment of stock landing in the country?
[aussman] 10kw for three phase is too small only provides 3.3kw per phase ovens at peak are 3.6, induction cookers are more and single phase hvac is is 4-5 so you would be paying for electricity even if your battery is full
[MilkteaS] 15kW 3P is 300 more than 10kW 3P. 10kW 3P is 300~400 more than 10kW 1P. If you prefer upgrading.
[ironpaw] EP11 is pretty old…I'd get CQ6/7 for self heating function especially if you're in Melbourne.
[MilkteaS] We have CQ7 as well😉
They are not here this time, as they are bit too big for many 1 car garages
[Lucille Bluth] Why Garage Installation?
For many homes, the garage can be one of the most practical places for a battery.
Depending on the property, garage installation may provide:
Protection from direct sun (hot) and weather (cold)
For FoxESS they have struggled for me during winter in Melbourne located outside. The charge rate is throttled if the temperature is below 10.9C. I had to build an enclosure which has fixed that. Previously I couldn't maximise the free charging period to fully charged my battery.
Checkout the FoxESS whirlpool page for similar complaints.
Get one with heating function. The one in this deal doesn't offer that.
[MilkteaS] True, this is another reason why we mentioned this as an garage sale: “ Protection from direct sun (hot) and weather (cold)”
The new slim one with heating (EP12-w) are coming soon, but they also come with a higher price.
[unco] Sorry if silly question but why is a bollard for single phase more expensive than a bollard for three phase?
[MilkteaS] I wonder why Gemini thought that too. Thank you for spot it out.
[c920996] More landfill after the warranty runs out??? What are your projected savings per house, per year?
[MilkteaS] If you're Victorian, you'll probably be happy to know the regulations prohibits any form of e-waste from entering landfill. . More than that, most battery have 6000 cycles of life so can use it easily for more than 15 years, which way longer than their 10 year warranty time. Australian Battery Recycling Initiative (ABRI) is the body who takes charge of this issue. In practice they would be send to recycling facilities.
Projected savings varies on the usage and use pattern. People using 100kWh per day clearly have different feels to people only use 10kWh.
